title: Right adjoints are unique up to a unique counit-compatible isomorphism
statement:
Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor with two right adjoints $G,J:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$,
with counits $\varepsilon^G:FG\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\varepsilon^J:FJ\to\mathrm{id}$. For
$K\in\mathcal D$ let $\gamma(K):GK\to JK$ be the $J$-transpose of
$\varepsilon^G(K):FGK\to K$, i.e. the unique morphism with
$\varepsilon^J(K)\circ F(\gamma(K))=\varepsilon^G(K)$, and let $\delta(K):JK\to GK$
be the $G$-transpose of $\varepsilon^J(K)$. Then $\gamma$ and $\delta$ are natural
transformations, mutually inverse, and $\gamma$ is the only natural
transformation $G\to J$ (indeed the only family of morphisms) compatible with
the counits.

mathlib_match.how: One Mathlib declaration per clause, with elementary identification by a Hom equivalence. For adjG : F ⊣ G and adjJ : F ⊣ J, take e = adjG.rightAdjointUniq adjJ (Unique.lean:102-103), a natural isomorphism G ≅ J. CategoryTheory.Adjunction.homEquiv_symm_rightAdjointUniq_hom_app (Unique.lean:105-108) says that the inverse adjJ.homEquiv sends e.hom.app K to adjG.counit.app K; hence e.hom.app K is exactly the prescribed gamma(K). CategoryTheory.Adjunction.homEquiv (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Basic.lean:160-171) is an equivalence whose inverse sends a to F.map a ≫ adjJ.counit.app K (line 163); the generated homEquiv_symm_apply, aliased as CategoryTheory.Adjunction.homEquiv_counit at line 182, is this formula. CategoryTheory.Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit (Unique.lean:127-130) is precisely the required counit equation. CategoryTheory.Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq_inv_app (Unique.lean:138-140) identifies e.inv.app K with (adjJ.rightAdjointUniq adjG).hom.app K; Unique.lean:105-108 instantiated with adj1 = adjJ and adj2 = adjG says (adjG.homEquiv (J.obj K) K).symm ((adjJ.rightAdjointUniq adjG).hom.app K) = adjJ.counit.app K. Thus e.inv.app K has precisely the defining G-transpose of delta(K), and injectivity of that equivalence identifies the two. Naturality and both inverse identities are the fields of e : G ≅ J. For any family a(K) with the required counit equation, (adjJ.homEquiv (G.obj K) K).symm a(K) = adjG.counit.app K = (adjJ.homEquiv (G.obj K) K).symm (e.hom.app K); injectivity of this equivalence gives a(K) = e.hom.app K separately for every K. This last uniqueness is a one-line application of equivalence injectivity and requires no naturality hypothesis.
